headline: The United Nations human rights chief warned that the world is running out of time to put guardrails on artificial intelligence.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an on-record speech by the UN's top human rights official, reported by the UN's own news service; it is a call for action, not a decision.
importance_line: It adds the UN's top human rights official to calls for binding AI rules and presses governments that host AI companies to act, which bears on anyone whose rights or services depend on automated systems, but a speech sets no rule and the accord is voluntary.
summary: UN News reports that Volker Türk, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, told a summit in Oxford on Monday 5 Oct that time is running out to put guardrails on AI, as a "ruthless race" between companies and countries raises safety concerns and a few control the tools without public oversight. He called for mandatory human rights safeguards and a ban on machines deciding who lives and who dies, and said that after new industry steps last week, which UN News says apparently refer to the voluntary White House accord of 29 Sep, too few are "walking the talk".
notes: UN News is the UN's own news service, reporting on its own official. The link to the 29 Sep White House accord is UN News's own reading ('apparently a reference'), kept hedged. Same article notes the New York City Council hearing held the same day (see C05-01).
